articles.title: स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति कौडीमा एनसेलले हात पारेपछि हंगामा, भुपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउपछि चासो बढ्यो
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। नेपाल प्रहरीको सीआइबीले भण्डारीलाई अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरेको छ। भण्डारी किन पक्राउ परे? स्मार्ट प्रकरणमा भण्डारीको भूमिका के? चासो देखिन्छन्।

नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणका पूर्वअध्यक्ष भूपेन्द्र भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका छन्। स्मार्ट सेलको सम्पत्ति बेचेर राज्यलाई हानी नोक्सानी पु¥याएको आरोपमा उनी पक्राउ परेका हुन्। तत्कालीन समयमा रेखा शर्मा सञ्चार तथा सूचना प्रविधिमन्त्री हुँदा भण्डारी विज्ञको रूपमा उनको सचिवालयमा नियुक्त भएका थिए ।

सचिवालयमा विज्ञ भनिएका भण्डारीलाई टेरामक्स प्रकरणले चिठ्ठा नै पर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। त्यसपछि टेरामक्स प्रकरणमा प्राधिकारणका तत्कालीन अध्यक्ष पुरुषोत्तम खनाल भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दाका कारण निलम्बित भएपछि उनले प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष पदमा सहजै पुग्ने स्थिति निर्माण गरे। तर, भण्डारी अध्यक्ष बनेपछि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा वेच्ने काम भएको बताइन्छ। राज्यको नाममा आईसकेको टेलिकमको सम्पत्तिलाई निजी कम्पनी एनसेललाई कौडीको भाउमा बेच्न सघाएको आरोपमा भण्डारी पक्राउ परेका हुन्।

के भन्यो सीआइबीले ?

नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)ले शुक्रबार ललितपुरको धापाखेलबाट पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ। उनलाई स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा अनुसन्धानका लागि पक्राउ गरिएको बताइएको छ। सीआईबीले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आएको स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति बेइमानीपूर्वक सरकारको हक टुटाउन काम गराएको आरोपमा भण्डारी माथि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको थियो।

दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट आधारभूत टेलिफोन सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न स्मार्ट टेलिकमले २०७० वैशाखमा अनुमति पाएको थियो। तर अनुमतिपत्र नवीकरण नगरेपछि स्मार्ट टेलिकमको लाइसेन्स स्वतः रद्द भएको थियो। यसरी सरकारको नाममा पुगिसकेको सम्पत्तिलाई बेचबिखन गर्नका निम्ति सघाएको आरोप भण्डारीमाथि समेत लागेको छ। प्राधिकरण नियामक निकाय समेत भएकाले पनि उनीमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने माग पहिलेदेखि नै उठ्दै आएको थियो । यता, ब्युरोले वैशाखमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमका तत्कालीन प्रबन्ध निर्देशक सर्वेश जोशीलाई पक्राउ गरिसकेको छ।

स्मार्टमा एनसेलको चलाखी

इजाजत खारेजीपछि विवादास्पद रूपमा सम्पत्ति लिलाम बिक्री भएको स्मार्ट टेलिकम प्रकरणमा निजी क्षेत्रको दूरसञ्चार सेवाप्रदायक कम्पनी एनसेल, त्यहाँका प्रमुख लगानीकर्ता र राजनीतिक नेतृत्वबीच शंकास्पद सम्बन्ध देखिएको भन्दै सीआइबीले अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ।

स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति बिक्रीबाट प्रमुख लाभग्राही एनसेल देखिएको छ। नेपाल दूरसञ्चार नियमावलीको नियम १० क मा एकै कम्पनीले एकभन्दा बढी दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकको अनुमति नपाउने उल्लेख छ। तर एनसेलमा लगानी गरेकाहरुले नै गैरकानुनीरूपले लिलामी गरिएको स्मार्ट टेलिकममा पनि लगानी सकारेकोे सीआईबीको ठहर छ ।

अहिले अनुसन्धानमा स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सेयर बिक्री, सेयर स्वामित्वको इतिहास, बैंक ऋण, सम्पत्ति हस्तान्तरण र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका विभिन्न कारोबार हेरिएको छ। प्रहरीले स्मार्ट टेलिकम, त्यसका सेयरधनी, सम्पत्ति व्यवस्थापन, उपकरण बिक्री र एनसेलसँग जोडिएका आर्थिक सम्बन्धबारे अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

सीआईबीका अनुसार सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रक्रियाभन्दा अगाडि नै स्मार्ट टेलिकम र एनसेलबीच सम्बन्ध देखिन्छ। यही आधारमा एनसेलसँग जोडिएका केही उच्च तहका व्यक्तिलाई पनि छानबिनको दायरामा ल्याइएको छ। स्मार्टको सम्पत्ति लिलाम प्रकरणमा एनसेलको नेपालस्थित सञ्चालकहरू सतिशलाल आचार्य, भावना सिंह श्रेष्ठ र सचिनलाल आचार्य पनि अनुसन्धानको राडारमै रहेका छन्।

दुरसञ्चार ऐन र स्वार्थको द्वन्द्ध

दुरसञ्चार ऐन २०५३ को दफा नंवर ३३ को उपदफा १ बमोजिम नेपाल सरकारले स्वामित्वमा आएको सम्पत्ति पूर्व अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिले उपदफा (३) बमोजिम निर्धारण गरिने मूल्य नेपाल सरकारलाई बुझाई पुनः अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरी दूरसञ्चार सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न सक्नेछ भनिएको छ ।

फेरि उपदफा २ बमोजिमको मूल्य निर्धारण गर्ने प्रयोजनको लागि नेपाल सरकारले प्राधिकरणको परामर्श लिई बमोजिम विशेषज्ञ व्यक्तिहरुको एक समिति गठन गर्न सक्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको छ । तर, प्राधिकारणले सरकारको स्वामित्वमा आइसकेको स्मार्ट टेलिकम एनसेललाई बेच्ने कुरा नै असंगत, पदीय दुरुपयोग र भ्रष्टाचार हुने दाबीहरु सार्वजनिक भइरहेका छन्।

यस्तो अवस्थामा प्राधिकरणको अध्यक्ष बनेका भण्डारीले पनि कानूनको उल्लङ्घन गर्दै स्मार्टको पक्षमा काम गरेकाले उनी अनुसन्धानमा तानिएका हुन्। तत्कालीन माओवादी केन्द्रबाट सञ्चारमन्त्री बनेकी शर्माले अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेका भण्डारीमाथि पदीय दुरुपयोगको गम्भीर आरोप लाग्दै गर्दा नियुक्ति दिने शर्मामाथि समेत केहिले प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। कतै यो सबै सेटिङमै त भएन?

प्रहरीले अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने बाटो यसतर्फ समेत केन्द्रित गर्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिन थालिएको छ। यद्यपी शर्मामाथि यस्ता आरोप भने सार्वजनिक रुपमा लागेको देखिन्न। तर, सचिवालयको विज्ञ भनिएको कर्मचारीलाई अध्यक्ष नियुक्त गरेपछि कानून मिचेको देखिदा उनीमाथि समेत यस्तो प्रश्न स्वभाविक बन्न पुगेको छ ।

articles.title: ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप नेपाल प्रवेश : जेम होम कलेक्सन आधिकारिक वितरक नियुक्त
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं। भारतको अग्रणी होम टेक्सटाइल कम्पनी ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा प्रवेश गरेको छ। कम्पनीले नेपालका लागि आफ्ना होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको एकमात्र आधिकारिक वितरकको रूपमा जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेडलाई नियुक्त गरेको घोषणा गरेको छ। यस सहकार्यसँगै नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अब ट्राइडेन्टका प्रिमियम बेड लिनेन, बाथ लिनेन, तौलियालगायतका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू आधिकारिक तथा भरपर्दो माध्यमबाट प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन्।

यसअघि नेपाली बजारमा ट्राइडेन्टका उत्पादनहरू प्रायः अनौपचारिक माध्यमबाट भित्रिने गरेकोमा यस नियुक्तिपछि गुणस्तर र प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितता हुने कम्पनीहरूको दाबी छ। यस साझेदारीले नेपालमा अन्तर्राष्ट्रियस्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरूको पहुँच विस्तार गर्ने र नेपाली ग्राहकहरूलाई विश्वस्तरीय गुणस्तर, आधिकारिक आपूर्ति शृंखला तथा उत्कृष्ट ग्राहक सेवा उपलब्ध गराउने लक्ष्य राखेको छ।

जेम होम कलेक्सन प्राइभेट लिमिटेड विगत ३० वर्षदेखि नेपालको फ्लोरिङ तथा फर्निसिङ क्षेत्रमा सक्रिय रहेको कम्पनी हो। यसले आतिथ्य र खुद्रा दुवै बजारका लागि विविध गुणस्तरीय उत्पादनहरू निरन्तर आपूर्ति गर्दै आएको छ। यही दीर्घकालीन बजार अनुभव र स्थापित वितरण सञ्जालका कारण कम्पनीलाई ट्राइडेन्टको आधिकारिक साझेदारका रूपमा छनोट गरिएको बताइएको छ।

ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपको स्थापना सन् १९९० मा भारतीय उद्यमी पद्मश्री राजिन्दर गुप्ताले पञ्जाबबाट सुरु गरेका थिए। सुरुमा एउटा मात्र धागो उत्पादन एकाइबाट सुरु भएको यो समूह हाल विश्वकै सबैभन्दा ठूला टेरी तौलिया उत्पादक र समग्र होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादकहरूमध्ये एक बनेको आर्थिक हिसाबले हेर्ने हो भने पछिल्लो प्रतिवेदन अनुसार ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुपले आर्थिक वर्ष २०२६ मा ६५ अर्ब २१ करोड भारतीय रुपैयाँ बराबरको आम्दानी हासिल गरेको थियो, जुन अघिल्लो वर्षको तुलनामा सामान्य घटेको भए पनि खुद नाफा भने बढेको थियो।

चालु आर्थिक वर्षको हालसालैको प्रगति हेर्दा पनि, पहिलो त्रैमासमा आम्दानी १ हजार ८ सय ३० करोड रुपैयाँ पुगेको र खुद नाफा ५५ प्रतिशतले वृद्धि भएको देखिन्छ। कम्पनीको समग्र आकारका सन्दर्भमा हेर्दा, ट्राइडेन्ट ग्रुप इन्डियामा हाल १६ हजार ३ सय तीनजना कर्मचारी कार्यरत रहेका छन् र यसको बजार पूँजीकरण करिब १।३२ बिलियन डलर बराबर रहेको पाइन्छ। समूह लामो समयदेखि आफूलाई एक बिलियन डलरभन्दा बढी मूल्यको वैश्विक व्यापारिक समूहको रूपमा चिनाउँदै आएको छ, जसको होम टेक्सटाइल, कागज र रसायन क्षेत्रमा सशक्त उपस्थिति रहेको दाबी गरिन्छ।

यसआधिकारिक वितरण सम्झौतापछि नेपाली उपभोक्ताहरूले अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरका होम टेक्सटाइल उत्पादनहरू प्रामाणिकताको सुनिश्चितताका साथ प्राप्त गर्न सक्नेछन् भने होटल तथा रिसोर्ट जस्ता आतिथ्य व्यवसायहरूले पनि विश्वसनीय आपूर्ति स्रोत भेट्टाउने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ। साथै यसले नेपालको होम फर्निसिङ बजारमा स्वस्थ प्रतिस्पर्धा र गुणस्तर सुधारमा समेत योगदान पुर्‍याउने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

articles.title: मेची राजमार्ग ठप्प ! सडक बन्द हुँदा बिरामीदेखि ढुवानीसम्म संकट
articles.summary:
इलाम । मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलाम माइखोला राजदुवालीकमाथि सडक अवरुद्ध भएको तीन सात भयो । सडक खुल्ने अझै छाँटकाँट छैन । सडक बन्द भएपछि इलाम मात्र हैन पुर्वी पहाडी जिल्ला पाँचथर ताप्लेजुङ लगायतका स्थानीयलाई समेत सास्ती भएको छ ।

मेची राजमार्ग अन्तर्गत इलामको माइखोला (राजदुवाली) माथिको सडक भासिएर तीन सातादेखि अवरुद्ध हुँदा इलामसँगै पाँचथर र ताप्लेजुङका नागरिकले सास्ती भोगिरहेका छन् । सडक बन्द भएपछि सवारी साधन वारिपारि नै रोकिने गरेका छन् भने यात्रुहरू करिब एक किलोमिटर भिरको बाटो पैदल हिँड्न बाध्य छन् ।

बिरामीलाई जनपथ प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी र नेपाली सेनाले स्टे«चरमार्फत वारपार गराइरहेका छन् भने एम्बुलेन्स पनि दुवैतर्फबाट सेवा दिन बाध्य छन् । अत्यावश्यक खाद्यान्न, ग्यास र तरकारी ढुवानीसमेत प्रभावित बनेको छ । इलाम नगरपालिकाले सरोकारवाला निकायसँग छलफल गरी पुनः इलामलाई संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरेको छ ।

राजदुवाली खण्डको पहिरो नियन्त्रण, ट्रस्ट पुल मर्मत तथा जोरकलश–हर्कटे सडक स्तरोन्नतिको लागि २४ करोड ९३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढीको ठेक्का जे एन्ड जे निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले २०८४ असारसम्म सम्पन्न गर्ने गरी लिएको भएपनि हालसम्म समग्रमा १८–२० प्रतिशत मात्र काम भएको सडक डिभिजन कार्यालयले जनाएको छ । स्थानीयले मुख्य सडकभन्दा वैकल्पिक सडक तत्काल सञ्चालनमा ल्याउन माग गरेका छन् ।

गत वर्ष तीन महिनासम्म संकटग्रस्त क्षेत्र घोषणा गरिए पनि प्रभावकारी काम नभएको भन्दै स्थानीय आक्रोशित छन् । सरकारले सडक बनाउन नसके इलामेली आफैंले श्रमदान र चन्दा उठाएर सडक तथा पुल निर्माण गर्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

सडक अवरुद्धकै कारण बिरामीले समयमै उपचार नपाएर ज्यान गुमाउनुपर्ने अवस्था रहेको भन्दै तत्काल समाधानको माग गरिएको छ ।

उता वैकल्पिक सडकका रूपमा प्रयोग गरिने सिमलगोलाई–तिल्केनी तथा केचना–कञ्चनजंघा सडकको बेलासी–भन्ज्याङ खण्ड पनि निर्माणमा ढिलाइका कारण सञ्चालन योग्य छैन । माइजोगमाई र पुवा खोलाका पुल गत वर्षको बाढीले बगाएपछि अहिलेसम्म पुनर्निर्माण हुन सकेको छैन । यस वर्ष बजेटमै इलामलाई बेवास्ता गरिएको भन्दै स्थानीयले सरकारसँग तत्काल सडक सञ्चालनको सुनिश्चितता गर्न माग गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: बौद्धनाथमा अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिमा राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप, कसले रोक्यो सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको नियुक्ति पत्र ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति तीन महिनादेखि अध्यक्षविहीन छ । संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालय मातहतको यो महत्वपूर्ण निकायमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको सिफारिस भइसके पनि राजनीतिक स्वार्थका कारण नियुक्तिले अझै पूर्णता पाउन सकेको छैन । अध्यक्ष नियुक्तिको निर्णय भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिँदा सरकारको नियतमाथि नै प्रश्न उठ्न थालेको छ ।

गत असार १८ गते मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयअनुसार संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्रालयले बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिको अध्यक्षमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामालाई नियुक्त गर्ने निर्णय गरेको थियो । तर विडम्बना, निर्णय भएको यति समय बितिसक्दा पनि लामाले नियुक्तिपत्र पाएका छैनन् ।

समितिका अध्यक्षसहित पाँच पदाधिकारी नियुक्त गरिए पनि अध्यक्ष लामाबाहेक सबै सदस्यले नियुक्तिपत्र बुझिसकेका छन् । अध्यक्षलाई मात्रै रोक्नुको कारण काठमाडौं–३ का रास्वपा सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे रहेको आरोप छ ।

स्थानीयका अनुसार सांसद पाण्डेले आफ्ना निकट व्यक्तिलाई अध्यक्ष बनाउन दबाब दिएपछि लामाको नियुक्तिपत्र रोकिएको हो । लामो समयदेखि समिति नेतृत्वविहीन हुँदा गुठियारदेखि स्थानीय सरोकारवालासम्म सरकारसँग जवाफ माग्न थालेका छन् । उनीहरूको चेतावनी छ, ‘रास्वपाभित्रको जुंगाको लडाइँको छायाँ बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिमा पार्न मिल्दैन ।’

दुई कार्यकाल सफलतापूर्वक अध्यक्षको जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका सम्पूर्णकुमार लामाको पुनः नियुक्तिका लागि गुठियार, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि, विभिन्न संघसंस्था र बुद्धिजीवीहरूले एकमत सिफारिस गरेका थिए । स्थानीयका अनुसार लामा सबैले स्वीकार गरेका र समन्वयकारी क्षमता भएका व्यक्ति हुन् । अध्यक्ष नहुँदा बौद्धनाथमा प्रशासनिक कामदेखि सामाजिक, धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा विकास निर्माणका गतिविधि प्रभावित भएका छन् । बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समितिले यहाँका विभिन्न धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक संघसंस्थाबीच समन्वय गर्दै आएको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका पनि अहिले नेतृत्व अभावकै कारण कमजोर बनेको छ ।

अलमलमा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा

अध्यक्षमा नियुक्ति भइसकेको एक महिना बित्न लाग्दा पनि नियुक्तिपत्र नपाउँदा सम्पूर्णकुमार लामा अन्योलमा परेका छन् । नियुक्ति भइसकेको व्यक्तिलाई नै बदर गराएर अर्को व्यक्तिलाई ल्याउने प्रयास सांसद पाण्डेले गरिरहेको स्थानीयको आरोप छ ।

उनीहरू भन्छन्, ‘सर्वस्वीकार्य व्यक्तिको नियुक्ति रोक्नु सरकारकै लागि ‘ब्याकफायर’ हुन सक्छ ।’ यसअघि पनि सरकार विभिन्न नियुक्ति र निर्णयका कारण विवादमा परिसकेको छ । धार्मिक तथा सांस्कृतिक संस्थामा राजनीतिक भागबन्डा होइन, योग्य र सबैले स्वीकार गर्ने व्यक्तिलाई नेतृत्व दिनुपर्ने स्थानीयको जोड छ । यही विषयलाई लिएर काठमाडौं–३ का सांसद राजुनाथ पाण्डे र संस्कृति, पर्यटन तथा नागरिक उड्डयन मन्त्री खडकराज पौडेल ९गणेश० बीच पनि मतभेद उत्पन्न भएको बताइएको छ ।

समितिका पाँच सदस्यमा विशाल लामा, निर्भिक्ता थिङ लामा, सेनाङ ग्याम्जो तामाङ, रोशनकुमार श्रेष्ठ र मणिभद्र पोखरेल नियुक्त भइसकेका छन् । तर अध्यक्षको नियुक्तिपत्र अझै रोकिँदा बौद्धनाथ क्षेत्र विकास समिति नेतृत्वविहीन अवस्थामै अल्झिएको छ र राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेपको आरोप झन् गहिरिँदै गएको छ ।

articles.title: पूजारी भन्छन्– बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको भ्रमले दर्शनार्थी घटे
articles.summary:
म्याग्दी । म्याग्दीको बेनी नगरपालिका ९ स्थित देशकै ऐतिहासिक र धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको गलेश्वरधाममा यस वर्षको साउन महिनामा विगतका वर्षको तुलनामा भक्तजनको चहलपहलमा कमि आएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यताका कारण पनि दर्शनार्थीहरुको कमी आएको हो ।

साउन महिना भगवान शिवको अत्यन्त प्रिय महिना भएकाले यस अवधिमा शिवको आराधना, रुद्राभिषेक, बेलपत्र चढाउने तथा जल चढाउनु विशेष फलदायी मानिन्छ । तर बृहस्पति अन्ध भएकै कारण मन्दिरमा दर्शन गर्न हुँदैन भन्ने भ्रम फैलिएको छ ।

बृहस्पति अन्ध रहेको अवधिमा शुभकार्य गर्न नहुने धार्मिक मान्यतालाई लिएर दर्शनसमेत गर्न नहुने भन्ने भ्रमका कारण भक्तजनको संख्या घटेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालयका गलेश्वरधामका मूल पुजारी चन्द्रमणि आचार्यका अनुसार धार्मिक शास्त्रमा भगवानको दर्शन र पूजा–अर्चना गर्न कुनै निषेध गरिएको छैन । बरु साउन महिनामा शिवको आराधना गर्दा विशेष पुण्य प्राप्त हुने धार्मिक विश्वास छ ।

गलेश्वरधाममा रहेको प्राकृतिक शिलामाथि अवस्थित स्वयं प्रकट शिवलिङ्ग विशेष आकर्षणको केन्द्र हो । एउटै ९ रोपनी क्षेत्रफलको विशाल चट्टानमाथि रहेको यो शिवलिङ्ग देश–विदेशका भक्तजनका लागि श्रद्धाको केन्द्र बनेको छ ।

विशेषगरी साउन महिना, महाशिवरात्रि, बालाचतुर्दशी तथा तीजका अवसरमा यहाँ हजारौँ श्रद्धालुको भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ ।

धेरै धार्मिक स्थलहरुमा पछि स्थापना गरिएको शिवलिङ्गमा पुजा गरिन्छ भने गलेश्वरधाममा स्वयं उत्पत्ती ज्योतिर्लिङ्ग भएको हुँदा पनि यस स्थानको छुट्टै धार्मिक महत्व हुने बताइन्छ ।

साउनको दोस्रो सोमबार भक्तजनले चढाएको भेटी गणना गरी बेनीस्थित गरिमा विकास बैंकमा दाखिला गरिएको छ । पहिलो सोमबार करिब दुई लाख रुपैयाँ भेटी संकलन भएको गलेश्वरधाममा दोस्रो सोमबार पनि करिब सोही हाराहारी रकम संकलन भएको थियो । भक्तजनको संख्या केही घटे पनि धार्मिक आस्थाका साथ दर्शन गर्ने क्रम भने निरन्तर भइरहेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र परिसरमा निर्माण गरिएको १०८ शिवलिङ्ग भक्तजनका लागि अर्को प्रमुख आकर्षण बनेको छ ।

गलेश्वर शिवालय क्षेत्र विकास कोषका उपाध्यक्ष बमबहादुर पुनको अगुवाइमा चन्दा तथा सहयोगबाट संकलित करिब साढे १३ लाख रुपैयाँमध्ये साढे ७ लाख रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर शिवलिङ्ग निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।

२०७६ सालमा निर्माण गरीएको यो धार्मिक महत्व दिने आकृति एकै स्थानमा १०८ शिवलिङ्गको दर्शन र पूजा गर्न सकिने भएपछि दैनिक रूपमा भक्तजन पुग्ने गरेका छन् ।

धार्मिक, सांस्कृतिक र प्राकृतिक सम्पदाको अनुपम संगमका रूपमा रहेको गलेश्वरधामले म्याग्दीको धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धनमा समेत महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ । २०८२ सालका चार वटा सोमबार गरी झण्डै १७ लाख रुपियाँ भेटी संकलन भएको थियो ।

articles.title: बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकामा भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा शुरु
articles.summary:
दोलखा । नेपालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहबाटै भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने व्यवस्था गरेको ११ वर्षपछि दोलखाको बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिकाले जिल्लामै पहिलो पटक भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखामार्फत मालपोत र नापीसम्बन्धी सेवा सञ्चालनमा ल्याएको छ ।

अब नागरिकले आफ्नै पालिकाबाट भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सेवा पाउने भएका छन् । २०७२ सालको संविधानले स्थानीय तहलाई भूमिसम्बन्धी सेवा प्रवाह गर्ने अधिकार दिएको थियो ।

त्यसलाई कार्यान्वयन गर्न नेपाल सरकारको भूमि व्यवस्था, सहकारी तथा गरिबी निवारण मन्त्रालय तथा संघीय मामिला तथा सामान्य प्रशासन मन्त्रालयले इच्छुक स्थानीय तहबाट आवेदन माग गरेपछि बैतेश्वर गाउँपालिका छनोटमा परेको हो ।

आवश्यक तयारी पूरा गरेपछि भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालय दोलखाले सेवा हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ । भूमि व्यवस्थापन शाखा सञ्चालनसँगै जग्गा किनबेच, नामसारी, अंशबण्डा, दानपत्र, हकछोड, सट्टापट्टा, नक्सा प्रिन्ट, कित्ता रेखाङ्कन लगायतका विभिन्न सेवा चरणबद्ध रूपमा गाउँपालिकाबाटै उपलब्ध हुने जनाइएको छ ।

सेवा लिन चाहने नागरिकमध्ये डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध भइसकेकाले पालिकाबाटै सेवा लिन सक्नेछन्। डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आबद्ध नभएकाले भने पहिलो पटक भूमि प्रशासन कार्यालयमा गई आफ्नो अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा दर्ता गराउनुपर्नेछ ।

नयाँ प्रणाली लागू भएसँगै सेवा नागरिकको घरदैलोमा पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिए पनि केही प्राविधिक चुनौती भने बाँकी नै छन् । भूमि प्रशासनसम्बन्धी सम्पूर्ण अभिलेख डिजिटल प्रणालीमा आधारित भएकाले श्रेस्ता (मूल अभिलेख) गाउँपालिकामा नहुँदा केही कानुनी तथा प्राविधिक जटिलता आउन सक्ने बताइएको छ । स्थानीय तहबाटै सेवा उपलब्ध हुन थालेपछि नागरिकको समय, खर्च र सदरमुकाम चरिकोट धाउनुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने भन्दै स्थानीय भने खुसी देखिन्छन् ।

संविधानले परिकल्पना गरेको स्थानीय तहबाट भूमि प्रशासन सेवा प्रवाहको व्यवस्था दोलखामा पनि कार्यान्वयनमा आएको हो । यसको प्रभावकारिता भने सेवा प्रवाहको गुणस्तर, डिजिटल प्रणालीको विश्वसनीयता र बाँकी प्राविधिक चुनौती समाधानमा निर्भर रहनेछ ।

articles.title: बुद्धकै पालादेखि शुरु भएको वर्षावास, किन शुरु भयो यस्तो परम्परा ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । असार पूर्णिमासँगै बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको तीन महिने वर्षावास सुरु भएको छ । गौतम बुद्धकै समयदेखि चल्दै आएको २५ सय वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आत्मअनुशासन, ध्यान, साधना र आध्यात्मिक उन्नतिको प्रतीक मानिन्छ । बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीहरूको अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण धार्मिक परम्परा तीन महिने वर्षावास शुरु भएको छ । हरेक वर्ष असार पूर्णिमादेखि कार्तिक पूर्णिमासम्म चल्ने यो परम्परा भिक्षुहरू एकै ठाउँमा बस्ने अभ्यास मात्रै होइन, यो अनुशासन, ध्यान, आध्यात्मिक साधना र बुद्धको जीवनसँग प्रत्यक्ष जोडिएको ऐतिहासिक अभ्यास पनि हो । बुद्धकै समयदेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्परा आखिर २५ सय वर्षपछि पनि किन उस्तै सान्दर्भिक छ ?

वर्षावासको सुरुवात

बुद्धले आफ्ना भिक्षुहरूलाई एउटा महत्वपूर्ण निर्देशन दिनुभएको थियो, “चरथ भिक्खवे चारिकं बहुजन हिताय, बहुजन सुखाय ।’ अर्थात्, “हे भिक्षुहरू ! बहुजनको हित र सुखका लागि गाउँ–गाउँ, नगर–नगर जाऊ, धर्म प्रचार गर ।’ बुद्धत्व प्राप्त गरेपछि भिक्षुहरू वर्षभरि विभिन्न स्थानमा धर्म प्रचार गर्न जान्थे । तर वर्षायाम सुरु भएपछि यात्रा कठिन हुन्थ्यो । बाटो बिग्रिन्थ्यो ।

नदीहरू बढ्थे । जीवजन्तु र बोटबिरुवामा क्षति पुग्ने सम्भावना पनि हुन्थ्यो । यही कारणले बुद्धले वर्षाको तीन महिना एकै स्थानमा बसेर ध्यान, अध्ययन र साधना गर्न निर्देशन दिनुभयो ।

यही अभ्यास नै पछि वर्षावासका रूपमा स्थापित भयो । धेरैलाई थाहा नहुन सक्छ, बौद्ध ग्रन्थमा उल्लेख भए अनुसार भगवान बुद्धले आफ्नो जीवनकालमा ४५ पटक वर्षावास बिताउनुभएको उल्लेख पाइन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष वर्षायाममा उहाँ कुनै न कुनै विहार, वन वा उपासकले बनाइदिएको आरामस्थलमा बस्नुहुन्थ्यो । यसले देखाउँछ, बुद्धले केवल उपदेश मात्र दिनुभएन । आफूले सिकाएको अभ्यासलाई जीवनभर पालना पनि गर्नुभयो ।

वर्षातको समयमा प्राकृतिक विपतिहरुबाट जोगिन र जोगाउनका साथै एकै ठाउँमा बसी नियमपुर्वक धार्मिक किसिमले जिवनयापन गर्नु नै यसको मुख्य उद्देश्य हो ।

वर्षावास किन विशेष छ ?

वर्षावास भिक्षुहरूको बसाइ मात्रै होइन । यो आत्मअनुशासनको समय हो । यस अवधिमा भिक्षुहरूले गहिरो ध्यान, विनयको अध्ययन, धर्म छलफल र आध्यात्मिक अभ्यासलाई प्राथमिकता दिन्छन् । उता गृहस्थ उपासक–उपासिकाहरू पनि विहारमा पुगेर दान, शील, ध्यान र धर्मश्रवणमार्फत आफ्नो आध्यात्मिक जीवनलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने प्रयास गर्छन् ।

वर्षावासपछि आउने कथिना चिवरदान

वर्षावास सकिएपछि बौद्ध समाजमा अर्को महत्वपूर्ण परम्परा सुरु हुन्छ कथिन चिवरदान । तीन महिना अनुशासित जीवन बिताएका भिक्षुहरूलाई श्रद्धालुहरूले सामूहिक रूपमा चिवर अर्पण गर्छन् । बौद्ध परम्परामा यसलाई सबैभन्दा ठूलो सामूहिक दानमध्ये एक मानिन्छ । यसले भिक्षु र गृहस्थबीचको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउने विश्वास गरिन्छ ।

बाइट–भिक्षु कौन्डण्य, विहार प्रमुख, बुद्ध विहार

विशेषगरी यो समयमा बौद्धमार्गीहरु विभिन्न विहारमा गई बुद्ध, धर्म, संघको गुणानुस्मरण गरी ध्यान भावना गरी आध्यात्मिक उन्नती तर्फ अग्रसर हुने गर्दछन् । विशेषगरी थेरवाद बुद्धधर्मको प्रभाव रहेको मुलुकमा वर्षावास परम्पराले धार्मिक आध्यात्मिक क्षेत्रमा सकारात्मक प्रभाव पारेको कारणले यसलाई बुद्धकालिन समयदेखि अहिलेसम्म पनि निरन्तरता दिइरहेको छ ।

२५ सय वर्षदेखि नटुटेको परम्परा

विश्वका धेरै धार्मिक अभ्यास समयसँगै परिवर्तन भएका छन् । तर वर्षावास भने बुद्धकालदेखि आजसम्म मूल स्वरूपमै कायम छ । नेपाल, श्रीलंका, थाइल्याण्ड, म्यानमार, कम्बोडिया, लाओस लगायत थेरवाद बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बी देशहरूमा आज पनि लाखौं भिक्षुहरू वर्षायाममा एकै स्थानमा बसेर यही परम्परा निर्वाह गर्छन् । समय फेरियो । प्रविधि फेरियो, समाज फेरियो । तर ध्यान, अनुशासन र आत्मशुद्धिको मूल्य कहिल्यै फेरिएन । सायद यही कारणले वर्षावास आज पनि उत्तिकै जीवित र सान्दर्भिक बनेको छ । बुद्धले सुरु गर्नुभएको वर्षावास अहिले एउटा धार्मिक अनुष्ठानमा मात्रै सिमित छैन ।

यो आत्मसंयम, करुणा, अनुशासन र आध्यात्मिक विकासको तीन महिने यात्राको रुपमा समेत स्थापित भइसकेको छ । बुद्धकै पालादेखि सुरु भएको यो परम्पराले आज पनि संसारभरका लाखौं बौद्ध अनुयायीलाई ध्यान, धर्म र आत्मपरिवर्तनतर्फ प्रेरित गरिरहेको छ ।

articles.title: घरभाडा व्यवस्थापन अब डिजिटल : घरधनी र भाडावालाको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्न ‘भाडासेवा’ बजारमा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालमा घर, फ्ल्याट, सटर तथा व्यावसायिक भवनको व्यवस्थापनलाई डिजिटल बनाउने उद्देश्यले एजिनेक्स क्लाउडले ‘भाडासेवा’ नामक क्लाउड–आधारित प्रणाली सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। ‘व्यवस्थित र सुमधुर सम्बन्धका लागि भाडासेवा’ मूल नारासहित आएको यो प्रणालीले कागजी अभिलेख र एक्सेल फाइलको झन्झट अन्त्य गर्दै घरभाडा व्यवस्थापनका सम्पूर्ण प्रक्रियालाई एकै डिजिटल प्लेटफर्ममा समेटेको छ।

यस प्रणालीमार्फत प्रयोगकर्ताले भवन तथा कोठाहरुको रियल–टाइम अनुगमन, भाडावालाको डिजिटल प्रोफाइल, अनलाइन सम्झौता र डिजिटल हस्ताक्षर गर्न सक्नेछन्। साथै, मासिक भाडा र बिजुली–पानीको बिल स्वतः तयार हुने, अनलाइन भुक्तानी गर्न मिल्ने तथा स्वचालित रसिद आउने सुविधा यसमा रहेको छ।

अपार्टमेन्ट तथा व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्सका साझा खर्च (CAM) व्यवस्थापन, मर्मतसम्भार ट्र्याकिङ, कर्मचारी व्यवस्थापन र आम्दानी–खर्चको विस्तृत रिपोर्टिङसमेत यसैबाट गर्न सकिन्छ।

साना घरधनीदेखि ठूला सपिङ मल र व्यावसायिक कम्प्लेक्ससम्मका लागि उपयोगी यो प्रणाली कम्प्युटर, ट्याब्लेट र मोबाइलबाटै सजिलै चलाउन सकिन्छ।

articles.title: इनड्राइभ नेपालद्वारा ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ प्रमाणपत्र प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं, नेपाल । विश्वव्यापी मोबिलिटी तथा डेलिभरी प्लेटफर्म इनड्राइभले महिलालाई ड्राइभिङ पेसामा अघि बढ्न समान अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरेको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रमको पहिलो चरण सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेको छ ।

कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत काठमाडौंमा आयोजित प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा तीन महिनाको प्रशिक्षण पूरा गरेका १० जना महिलालाई सम्मान गरिएको छ । सुरक्षित र आत्मनिर्भर रूपमा दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारी चलाउने पेसामा अघि बढ्न आवश्यक सीप, आत्मविश्वास र स्रोतसाधन प्रदान गर्ने उद्देश्यले सहभागीहरूलाई विभिन्न चरणमा प्रशिक्षण दिइएको थियो ।

अप्रिल २०२६ मा सुरु भएको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रम विशेषगरी अवसरबाट वञ्चित समुदायका महिलालाई मोबिलिटी क्षेत्रमा आर्थिक अवसरमा पहुँच दिलाउने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरिएको हो । महिलालाई परम्परागत रूपमा पुरुषको वर्चस्व रहेको पेसामा प्रवेश गर्न बाधा पु¥याउने सामाजिक तथा व्यावहारिक अवरोधलाई कम गर्न पनि कार्यक्रमले जोड दिएको छ ।

प्रशिक्षण अवधिभर सडक सुरक्षालाई व्यावसायिक दक्षताको महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । सहभागीहरूलाई व्यावहारिक राइडिङ प्रशिक्षणसँगै सडक सुरक्षासम्बन्धी मार्गदर्शन प्रदान गर्नुका साथै औपचारिक सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र (लाइसेन्स) प्राप्त गर्ने प्रक्रियामा समेत सहयोग गरिएको थियो ।

प्रत्येक सहभागीलाई सुरक्षात्मक हेल्मेट तथा प्राथमिक उपचार र स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी सामग्रीसहितको सुरक्षा किट प्रदान गरिएको थियो ।

व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षालाई पनि प्रशिक्षणको छुट्टै महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । फाइटब्याक नेपाल सँगको सहकार्यमा उन्नत आत्मरक्षा तालिम सञ्चालन गरिएको थियो, जसले सहभागीहरूलाई सम्भावित सुरक्षा चुनौती पहिचान गर्न, आत्मविश्वास बढाउन र आवश्यक अवस्थामा व्यवहारिक रूपमा सामना गर्न सक्ने सीप विकास गर्न सहयोग गरेको थियो ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यका ट्राफिक प्रहरी कार्यालयका डीएसपी सुनिलजंग शाहले भने, “सडक सुरक्षा सबैको साझा जिम्मेवारी हो र यसमा प्रत्येक चालकको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका हुन्छ । हामी सहभागीहरूलाई ट्राफिक नियमको पालना गर्न, सडकमा सधैं सचेत रहन र अनुभव बढाउँदै निरन्तर सिकिरहन आग्रह गर्छौं । सबै सहभागीलाई बधाई दिँदै व्यावसायिक चालकका रूपमा उनीहरूको सुरक्षित र सफल यात्राका लागि शुभकामना व्यक्त गर्दछौं ।”

मोबिलिटीमा महिलाको पहुँच विस्तार यस समूहका महिलाका लागि सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र केवल आम्दानीको माध्यम मात्र नभई आफ्नो काम, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य सेवा तथा बजारसम्म आफ्नै समयअनुसार स्वतन्त्र रूपमा पुग्ने अवसर पनि हो । यसले सार्वजनिक यातायातको समयतालिका वा परिवारका अन्य सदस्यमा निर्भर रहनुपर्ने अवस्थालाई कम गर्न सहयोग पु¥याउँछ ।

दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारीमा आधारित राइड–हेलिङ सेवाले चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारी पुग्न कठिन हुने साँघुरा गल्ली तथा अन्तिम गन्तव्यसम्म पनि सेवा पु¥याउन सक्छ । सामान्यतया यसको भाडा पनि चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारीको तुलनामा कम हुने गर्दछ । राइड–हेलिङ सेवामा महिलाको सहभागिता बढ्दा यात्रुहरूले आफूलाई उपयुक्त चालक छनोट गर्ने थप अवसरसमेत पाउनेछन् ।

प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोह प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा साझेदार संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि, सरकारी निकायका सरोकारवाला, सञ्चारकर्मी तथा विशिष्ट अतिथिहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो ।

समारोहमा इनड्राइभका प्रतिनिधि तथा इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले कार्यक्रम सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेका १० जना सहभागीलाई प्रमाणपत्र, सुरक्षा किट तथा मायाको चिनो प्रदान गरे । कार्यक्रममा सहभागी १० जना महिलाको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ यात्रालाई समेटिएको भिडियोसमेत प्रदर्शन गरिएको थियो ।

समारोहका क्रममा सहभागीमध्ये एक जनालाई विद्युतीय स्कुटर, तीन जनालाई स्मार्टफोन र छ जनालाई स्मार्टवाच प्रदान गरिएको थियो । यी सामग्रीले उनीहरूलाई व्यावसायिक ड्राइभिङ यात्राको सुरुवातमा थप सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।

इनड्राइभ साउथ एसियाकि कम्युनिकेसन म्यनाजर शेरिन एर्विना कौरले भनिन्, “हामीले विभिन्न बजारमा एउटै अवस्था देखिरहेका छौं, राइड माग्ने यात्रुमध्ये धेरै महिला छन्, तर उनीहरूलाई राइड दिने चालकमा महिलाको संख्या निकै कम छ । यो महिलाले यस्तो काम गर्न चाहन्छन् कि चाहँदैनन् भन्ने विषय थिएन। मुख्य प्रश्न उनीहरूका लागि यो पेसामा प्रवेश गर्ने बाटो उपलब्ध थियो कि थिएन भन्ने थियो । नेपालमा सञ्चालन गरिएको पहिलो समूहले तालिम, लाइसेन्स र प्लेटफर्ममा पहुँचलाई एउटै यात्राका रूपमा जोड्दा कस्तो परिवर्तन सम्भव हुन्छ भन्ने देखाएको छ। हामी अन्य बजारमा पनि यसबाट सिक्दै कार्यक्रमलाई अघि बढाउनेछौं ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी कम्युनिकेसन्स म्यानेजर मञ्जिता गुरुङले भनिन्, “सीप विकास तालिम यस यात्राको एउटा हिस्सा मात्र हो । सामाजिक सोच र धारणाले पनि उत्तिकै महत्व राख्छ, र महिलाले ड्राइभिङ सुरु गरेपछि उनी प्रवेश गर्ने वातावरण पनि महत्वपूर्ण हुन्छ । ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलालाई लाइसेन्स प्राप्त गर्नेदेखि आत्मविश्वास विकास गर्ने, परिवारमा यसबारे संवाद गर्ने र आम्दानीको अवसर सिर्जना गर्नेसम्म हरेक पक्षमा सहयोग गर्ने गरी तयार गरिएको हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरू यो पेसामा आउँछन्, यात्रुहरूले पनि लाभ पाउँछन्, उनीहरूसँग आफूलाई राइड गराउने चालक छनोट गर्ने थप विकल्प हुन्छ ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी सिनियर ड्राइभर अपरेसन्स स्पेसलिस्ट सुनिता जीमी राईले भनिन्, “इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलाका लागि थप सहयोगी वातावरण निर्माण गर्ने दिशामा महत्वपूर्ण कदम हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरूले सवारीको स्टेयरिङ समाउँछन्, उनीहरूले नेपाललाई थप समावेशी भविष्यतर्फ अघि बढाउन पनि भूमिका खेलिरहेका हुन्छन् ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले भनिन्, “‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ ले अन्यायलाई चुनौती दिँदै समुदायमा सकारात्मक परिवर्तन ल्याउने इनड्राइभको प्रतिबद्धतालाई प्रतिबिम्बित गर्छ । मानिस र समानतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर अघि बढाइएको यस पहलको हिस्सा बन्न पाउँदा म गर्व गर्छु ।”

articles.title: पार्टी निर्माणमा सि जिनपिङको अवधारणाबारे नेपालमा चर्चा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित विश्वमा राजनीतिक दलको निर्माण र त्यसको प्रभावकारी संचालनका लागि चिनियाँ राष्ट्रपति सि जिनपिङको अवधारणा उपयोगी हुने विज्ञहरुले बताएका छन् । फ्रेन्डस अन क्लाउडले काठमाडौंमा गरेको कार्यक्रममा राजनीतिज्ञ जगन्नाथ खतिवडा, परराष्ट्रविद डा गोपाल खनाल, पूर्व राजदूत महेशराज दाहाल, अनुसन्धानकर्ता डा। दीपक देवकोटा र क्लाउडका अध्यक्ष शोभित उप्रेतीले पार्टी निर्माणमा राष्ट्रपति सी का विभिन्न आयामबारे धारणा राखेका हुन् ।

कार्यक्रममा बो्ल्दै पूर्व राजदूत दाहालले राष्ट्रपति सिको अध्ययनशिल बानी नै पार्टी र राष्ट्र निर्माणका लागि आधारशिला बनेको उल्ले गरे ।

दाहालका अनुसार श्रम शिविरमा हुँदा पनि निकै अध्धयन गर्ने सी लामो र नयाँ सोचका थिए । सृजनशीलता परिवर्तनकारी सोचका धनी सीले पार्टी सदसयता पाउन पनि निकै संघर्ष गरेकाले पार्टी कस्तो हुनुपर्छ भन्ने पनि उनले राम्रोसँग बुझेका थिए ।

राम्रो दृष्टिकोण भए पार्टी र देश बन्छ भन्ने कुरा उनले प्रमाणित गरेर देखाए । भ्रष्टाचार विरुद्वका कार्यक्रम र दल भित्रको शुद्वतामा उनको जोड थियो । नेतृत्वको जिम्मेवारी र कर्तव्य । प्रविधि विकास, जनताको सहभागीता, विज्ञानमा लगानी उनको पार्टी निर्माणका प्रमुख साधन हुन ।

यस्तै , डा दिपक देवकोटाले राष्ट्रपति सीले राज्यबाट डर नभई भरोसा जगाउने काम गरेर सफलता प्राप्त गरेको धारणा राखे । जनतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर पार्टी र देश निर्माण गर्न उनी सफल भए ।

जनताले विश्वास गर्ने पार्टी बनाउन राष्ट्रपति सी ले सुशासन र सुरक्षालाई प्राथमिकता दिएको उनले बताए । परराष्ट्र विद डा गोपाल खनालले विश्वव्यापी सुशासन अभियान र नयाँ युगका लागि चिनियाँ विशेषतासहितको समाजवाद नै सि जिनपिङको पार्टी निर्माणको स्पष्ट अवधारणा भएको बताए ।

पार्टी नियम र देश कानुनबाट चल्छ भन्ने कुरा राष्ट्रपति सी ले स्थापित गरेको उनको भनाइ छ । जनतालाई विकास दिने सोच नै सिको सोच भएको खनालको निष्कर्ष छ।

आर्थिक अनियमितता गर्ने ७० लाख भन्दा बढीलाई चीनमा कारबाही गरिएको जानकारी दिंदै खनालले राष्ट्रपति सी को सुशासन अभियानको प्रशंसा गरे ।

नेता जगन्नाथ खतिवडाले अनुशासन, अनुगमन र आत्मसमीक्षाको सुत्र न‌ै राष्ट्रपति सि को पार्टी र देश निर्माणको आधारशिला रहेको धारणा राखे ।

राष्ट्रपति सि ले विचार निर्माण, राजनीति निर्माण र संगठन निर्माणमा जोड दिंदै पार्टीमा गुणस्तरीय सदस्यलाई मात्र स्थान दिएको खतिवडाले बताए । चीन जस्तो शक्तिशाली राष्ट्र हाम्रो छिमेकी भएकाले दलीय एकता तथा दीर्घकालीन सोच र योजनाका साथ अघि बढ्ने कुरा नेपालले सिक्नुपर्ने खतिवडा बताउँछन् ।

articles.title: ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंकमा नागरिक एपबाटै खाता खोल्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक लिमिटेडले नागरिक एपसँगको सहकार्यमा नागरिक एपमार्फतै बैंक खाता खोल्न सकिने नयाँ सुविधा सुरु गरेको छ ।

राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्रका आधारमा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध नेपाली नागरिकले बैंकको वेबसाइटमा उपलब्ध क्यूआर कोड स्क्यान गरी व्यक्तिगत बचत खाता अनलाइनबाटै खोल्न सक्नेछन् ।

यो सेवा १८ वर्ष वा सोभन्दा माथिका राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र भएका तथा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध व्यक्तिका लागि उपलब्ध हुनेछ । खाता खोल्ने क्रममा बैंकले ग्राहकको पूर्वसहमतिमा आवश्यक व्यक्तिगत विवरण नागरिक एपबाट सुरक्षित रूपमा प्राप्त गर्ने भएकाले पुनः विवरण भर्नुपर्ने झन्झट हट्ने, गोपनीयता कायम रहने र सूचनाको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित हुने बैंकले जनाएको छ ।

नागरिक एपमार्फत खोलिएको खाता सञ्चालनका लागि भने ग्राहकले नजिकको शाखामा गई वा भिडियो केवाईसीमार्फत प्रमाणीकरण गर्नुपर्नेछ ।

बैंकका अनुसार सरकारी डिजिटल पूर्वाधारको उपयोग गर्दै सुरु गरिएको यो सेवाले खाता खोल्ने प्रक्रियालाई थप सहज, सुरक्षित, पारदर्शी र प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनेछ । ग्राहकलाई आधुनिक डिजिटल बैंकिङ अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास बैंकको छ ।

ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक ७७ वटै जिल्लामा शाखा सञ्जाल विस्तार गर्ने निजी क्षेत्रको पहिलो वाणिज्य बैंक हो ।

हाल बैंकले ३४२ शाखा, ३६८ एटिएम, १४७ शाखारहित बैंकिङ सेवा, ६९ एक्सटेन्सन तथा राजस्व सङ्कलन काउन्टर र ३ वटा वैदेशिक प्रतिनिधि कार्यालयसहित १ हजारभन्दा बढी सेवा केन्द्रमार्फत सेवा दिँदै आएको छ ।

articles.title: मेलम्चीमा स्थानीय उत्पादन प्रवर्द्धनका लागि ‘कोशेली घर’ उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
मेलम्ची । स्थानीय कृषि र हस्तकला उत्पादनलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने उद्देश्यले सिन्धुपाल्चोकको मेलम्ची बजारमा नयाँ व्यावसायिक केन्द्र “कोशेली घर” सञ्चालनमा आएको छ। साउन ८ देखि हरेक दिन बिहान ७ बजेदेखि राति ७ बजेसम्म खुल्ने यो कोशेलीघरको उद्घाटन नगरप्रमुख आइतमान तामाङले गरेका छन् ।

नगरप्रमुख तामाङले कोशेलीघरबाट ताजा फलफूल तथा तरकारी, घरेलु अचार, मह, भान्साका आवश्यक परिकार, हस्तकला सामग्री, अण्डा, माछा, गेडागुडी, चिया, कफी तथा हर्बल सामग्रीलगायत स्थानीय रैथाने उत्पादनको सीधा बिक्री वितरणमा जोड दिने बताए । उनले यहाँ राखिने विशेष परिकार तथा उत्पादनहरू आवश्यक परेमा जिल्ला बाहिर पनि पठाइने समेत जनाए ।

कोशेलीघरले स्थानीय उत्पादक र उपभोक्तालाई एउटै छानामुनि प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाटको व्यवस्था गराउँदै बजारसम्म पहुँच सहज बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको प्रमुख तामाङले बताए ।

साथै प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत निमेष मिश्रले ‘फार्म देखि किचनसम्म अवधारणाअनुरूप उत्पादक र उपभोक्ताको मागअनुसार नयाँ वस्तु तथा उत्पादनहरू परिष्कृत गरी सार्वजनिक गरिने र उद्यमीहरूको भेटघाट हुने उपयुक्त स्थलको रूपमा यसलाई विकास गर्ने योजना रहेको बताए । प्रारम्भिक अनुमान अनुसार नगरपालिकाले दैनिक हजारौंले यहाँबाट किनमेल गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

मेलम्ची आसपासका सरकारी तथा निजी कार्यालयका कर्मचारी, घुम्न आउने पर्यटक, स्थानीय टोल तथा छिमेकी पालिकाका बासिन्दाहरू प्रमुख लक्षित ग्राहक रहने कोशेलीघरबाट स्थानिय रोजगारी र व्यवसायिक गतिविधिलाई थप सक्रिय बनाउन मद्दत पुग्ने उपस्थित उपभोक्ताले विश्वास व्यक्त गरिएको थियो ।

articles.title: Broad Peak avalanche wipes out a generation of Nepali climbing greats
articles.summary:
When a massive avalanche swept down Pakistan’s 8,051-metre Broad Peak on Thursday morning, it did more than claim six Nepali lives. It wiped out one of the most accomplished generations of high-altitude climbers the country has produced, taking with it decades of technical expertise, leadership and record-breaking achievement.

Among those killed was world-renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja, widely known as Nimsdai, along with five elite Nepali mountain guides whose experience and skills helped shape modern Himalayan climbing.

According to Nepali expedition operators and mountaineering entrepreneurs, the country has rarely suffered such a concentrated loss of internationally recognised and highly accomplished climbers in a single mountain disaster.

The other Nepali climbers killed in the avalanche were Pur Bahadur Gurung, also known as Yukta; Kili Pemba Sherpa, known as Kilu; Nima Sherpa; Nawang Thendu Sherpa; and Gyaljen Sherpa, known as Gyalu. Most had completed dozens of successful ascents of Everest and other 8,000-metre peaks, with several earning global recognition for their achievements.

Gyalu Sherpa and Nawang Thendu Sherpa were associated with Seven Summit Treks. Pur Bahadur Gurung and Nima Sherpa were senior guides with Nimsdai’s Elite Exped, while Kili Pemba Sherpa was a lead guide with Imagine Nepal.

Gyalu Sherpa, a veteran climber from Okhaldhunga, began his commercial mountaineering career in 2015. Over the years, he built an impressive climbing résumé, summiting Lenin Peak, Mera Peak, Lobuche, Himlung Himal, Cholatse, Manaslu, Kanchenjunga and Everest.

Kanchenjunga held particular significance for him. Earlier this year, he completed another successful ascent of Everest after repeatedly summiting the world’s third-highest peak.

“Gyalu set a Guinness World Record by summiting Kanchenjunga three times in a single season, and he climbed Everest many times,” said Chhang Dawa Sherpa, director of Seven Summit Treks, adding that Gyalu had worked with the company for nearly eight years.

Chhang Dawa said 29-year-old Nawang Thendu Sherpa, who was unmarried, had also begun his professional climbing career with Seven Summit Treks and had quickly established himself as a dependable high-altitude guide.

Among those killed, Kili Pemba Sherpa stood out as one of Nepal’s most accomplished mountaineers.

He was one of the 10 elite Nepali climbers led by Nimsdai who made history on January 16, 2021 by completing the first winter ascent of K2, the world’s second-highest mountain and widely regarded as one of its most technically demanding peaks.

Only weeks before the Broad Peak tragedy, on July 3, Kili Pemba reached the summit of Pakistan’s 8,126-metre Nanga Parbat, completing all 14 of the world’s 8,000-metre peaks. Less than a month after achieving that milestone, he was killed in the avalanche on Broad Peak.

The recovery of his body on Friday sent shockwaves through the Rolwaling Valley in Dolakha, where he was born, and across the international mountaineering community.

Born in 1980 into a modest family in Beding, Gaurishankar Rural Municipality-9, Kili Pemba began working on mountaineering expeditions at the age of 16, joining a Manaslu expedition in 1996 as a support worker.

Although his first attempt to reach the summit ended in failure, the experience strengthened his determination. After years of building technical expertise on smaller peaks, he successfully climbed Manaslu in 2002 and reached the summit of Everest for the first time the following year.

Kili Pemba’s contributions extended well beyond his own climbing record.

In 2021, alongside Mingma Gyalje Sherpa, known as Mingma G, he helped identify the true summit route on Manaslu, resolving a long-standing issue under which many climbers had stopped at a fore-summit instead of the mountain’s highest point. The route they identified has since become the accepted line for expeditions.

He also earned international fame for guiding climbers with disabilities on some of the world’s highest mountains. In 2018, he led Chinese double amputee Xia Boyu to the summit of Everest, and in 2021 guided Russian double amputee Rustam Nabiev to the top of Manaslu.

According to his uncle, Dawa Chirring Sherpa, Kili Pemba had successfully summited Everest 15 times during his career, earning a reputation as one of Nepal’s most skilled and dependable high-altitude guides.

Nima Sherpa, from Chyakse Boda in Makalu Rural Municipality-2 of Sankhuwasabha, was widely regarded as a disciplined, honest and fearless climber. Raised in a farming family, he built a reputation as a dependable high-altitude guide. Working with Elite Exped, Nima had successfully climbed four 8,000-metre peaks this year before joining the Broad Peak expedition.

Pur Bahadur Gurung, widely known as Yukta, had travelled to Pakistan three weeks earlier with the aim of climbing K2. That plan changed after one of his clients broke an arm, forcing the expedition to postpone its K2 attempt. He then joined Nimsdai’s Broad Peak team.

Yukta had already climbed 12 of the world’s 14 mountains above 8,000 metres, leaving his ambition of completing all 14 unfinished.

Three years ago, after completing his seventh ascent of Everest in May, he spoke of his enduring passion for the mountains.

“The moment I head for the mountains, my spirit soars; standing on the summit fills me with pure energy,” he said in an interview.

A native of Laprak in Dharche Rural Municipality-4, Gorkha, Yukta came from a village known for producing accomplished climbers. Six people from Laprak have set records on Everest. He also became the first climber from the Gurung community to summit Everest 10 times.

He first reached the world’s highest peak in 2011 at the age of 22 and completed his tenth ascent on May 20 this year. His climbing record also included successful ascents of Makalu, Annapurna, Lhotse and K2.

Confirmation that his body had been recovered alongside that of Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy plunged Laprak into mourning.

Nawang Thendu Sherpa was among the youngest guides killed in the avalanche. Though only 29 and unmarried, he had already scored an impressive climbing record, having summited Everest, Lhotse, Manaslu, Kanchenjunga, Makalu and Ama Dablam.

He first climbed Everest in 2022 and reached the summit of Makalu earlier this year.

According to Ongdi Tshering Sherpa, chairman of Makalu Rural Municipality, Nawang came from a family deeply rooted in mountaineering. His father and three brothers are all veteran climbers who have summited 8,000-metre peaks.

“Nawang’s passing deprives our village of a courageous, honest and exceptionally promising young man,” Ongdi said. “His contributions, discipline and dedication will be remembered by Nepal’s mountaineering fraternity for years to come.”

Leaders in Nepal’s mountaineering industry said the deaths represent more than a personal tragedy, warning that the loss of such an experienced group of climbers will have lasting consequences for the country’s adventure tourism sector.

“An international-standard mountain guide cannot be produced overnight,” said Chhang Dawa, director of Seven Summit Treks.

“It takes years of training, repeated expeditions and practical experience. Companies like ours recruit young men from remote Himalayan villages, train them over many seasons and help them become world-class professionals. Losing climbers of this calibre is a devastating blow, not only for Nepal but also for the global mountaineering community.”

articles.title: India’s sugar export ban fuels smuggling ahead of peak festival season
articles.summary:
Sugar smuggling along Nepal’s southern border has surged after India imposed a fresh ban on the export of the sweetener more than two months ago, raising concerns over illegal trade in the run-up to the September-October festival season.

Sugar seizures by the Armed Police Force increased by more than twofold between mid-June and mid-July, the Nepali month of Asar, compared to the previous month. The police force assigned with border security confiscated 10 tonnes of smuggled sugar worth Rs780,255 during the period, up from 4 tonnes worth Rs284,870 in the previous month.

On Sunday alone, the APF confiscated 32 sacks of sugar smuggled from Jhapa district in eastern Nepal. Netra Bahadur Karki, spokesperson and deputy inspector general, Armed Police Force, said most of the confiscated sugar was intercepted in Tarai-Madhesh districts along the Indian border.

India banned sugar exports on May 13 until September 30, 2026, or until further notice. The world’s second-largest sugar producer imposed the ban to contain domestic prices amid concerns that El Niño conditions could lead to drought, reduce sugarcane output and lower next season’s sugar production.

Sugar prices in Nepal have increased by around Rs15 per kg since India imposed the ban. Sugar that sold for around Rs95 per kg now costs around Rs110 in most retail outlets.

Consumer rights groups say the government failed to act quickly after India announced the export ban.

“The issues of supply, pricing and market management of essential commodities have not been addressed by the government, just as they were ignored by previous administrations. It is surprising that the government has remained silent as if nothing is wrong,” said Prem Lal Maharjan, president of the National Consumer Forum.

“With the festive season approaching, the government still has no clear supply management policy. It should ensure sufficient stocks so that traders cannot exploit the situation through black marketing and price hikes,” Maharjan said.

Activists say the rise in sugar smuggling not only deprives the government of customs revenue but also raises concerns about the quality and safety of illegally imported sugar.

The Salt Trading Corporation said it currently has 1,677 tonnes of sugar in stock but has yet to receive any government directive to procure additional supplies.

The state-owned corporation is selling sugar at Rs100 per kg. More than a month ago, it was selling sugar at Rs98 per kg after purchasing supplies from the private sector.

According to the corporation, Nepal’s monthly sugar demand ranges between 20,000 and 25,000 tonnes and rises to around 30,000 tonnes during major festivals such as Dashain, Tihar and Chhath.

Annual demand is estimated at about 300,000 tonnes, while domestic production falls short by about 100,000 tonnes, making imports necessary to meet consumption.

Netra Subedi, joint secretary at the Ministry of Industry, said the Food Management and Trading Company (FMTC) is importing 1,000 tonnes of sugar, which has already arrived in Nepalgunj.

“Once the current stock is sold, FMTC will decide how much more sugar to import based on market demand,” Subedi said.

The Ministry of Industry has decided to import sugar through a government-to-government agreement with India.

“We still have a remaining quota of 10,000 tonnes under the allocation India approved in September last year, and we are importing sugar under that quota,” Subedi said.

Last year, Nepal had requested permission to import 60,000 tonnes of sugar to meet festive demand, but India approved only 25,000 tonnes through the National Cooperative Exports Limited.

Kumar Rajbhandari, deputy chief executive officer of the Salt Trading Corporation, said the state-owned food companies did not import sugar last year under the quota because import costs, including customs duties, exceeded prevailing market prices.

“After paying customs duties, imported sugar became more expensive than the market price, so we decided not to import it,” Rajbhandari said. The corporation has been requesting the government to provide subsidies on sugar imports so that they can sell below prevailing market prices.

Nepal Sugar Mills Association said that Nepal produced 180,000 tonnes of sugar from last year’s harvest. The production is expected to increase by 215,000 tonnes this year.

The association said that it had a stock of 80,000 tonnes of sugar a month ago.

Sugar imports increased by 90.16 percent in the last fiscal year compared with the previous fiscal year 2024-25.

According to the Department of Customs, Nepal imported 51,485 tonnes of sugar worth Rs3.48 billion during the last fiscal year.

India had previously suspended sugar exports to Nepal in September 2023 after poor rainfall reduced sugarcane yields. The restriction was later extended beyond October 31, coinciding with Nepal’s peak festive season and triggering a sharp spike in prices. Ahead of Dashain that year, sugar prices rose from around Rs88 per kg to as high as Rs160 per kg in the black market amid shortages.

articles.title: Policy uncertainty hit economy as stocks and imports suffer most
articles.summary:
Uncertainty in government’s economic policies has a significant negative impact on the country’s economy, with the stock market and imports among the worst affected.

According to a new study, titled Macroeconomic Effects of Economic Policy Uncertainty: Evidence from Nepal, by the Nepal Rastra Bank, growing uncertainty over fiscal and monetary policies weakens economic activity, discourages investment and affects financial markets. It estimates that prolonged policy uncertainty can reduce the Nepal Stock Exchange (Nepse) index by as much as 10 percent, real imports by 15 percent, private sector credit by 5 percent and gross domestic product (GDP) by around 2 percent.

The working paper was prepared by central bank officials Birendra Bahadur Budha and Rohan Byanjankar, along with researcher Swastik Nepal. It is the first study to develop an Economic Policy Uncertainty Index specifically for Nepal.

The researchers constructed the index using real-time Google trends data covering the period from January 2011 to April 2026. The index measures the frequency of internet searches related to economic policy uncertainty. A rise in searches for uncertainty-related terms is interpreted as growing concern among households, businesses and investors about the country's economic policy direction.

The findings come at a time when economists and the private sector have increasingly questioned frequent policy changes by successive governments and regulators, arguing that abrupt revisions undermine business confidence. In recent years, both fiscal and monetary policies have been amended repeatedly after implementation, often in response to criticism from businesses and other stakeholders.

According to the report, the stock market reacts almost immediately to policy uncertainty. Investors tend to sell shares as uncertainty increases because it becomes more difficult to predict future returns and assess investment risks.

"The impact of policy uncertainty is observed most rapidly in the Nepse index," the report says. "Immediately after an uncertainty shock, the index falls by around 5 percent, while the maximum decline reaches about 10 percent if uncertainty persists."

The study also found that uncertainty is typically highest during the period when the government prepares and announces the annual budget and when the central bank unveils its monetary policy.

Until 2015, Nepal generally presented its annual budget in mid-June. Since then, the budget has been announced on 15 of Nepali month of Jestha (which was May 29 this year), while the Nepal Rastra Bank usually releases its monetary policy towards the end of mid-July. The report identifies these periods as the most sensitive for policy-related uncertainty.

The index also recorded notable spikes during the 2014 South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) Summit in Kathmandu and the 2018 Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) Summit. Another sharp increase was observed in 2022, when Nepal's foreign exchange reserves came under severe pressure, prompting concerns over external sector stability.

Beyond financial markets, the study suggests that policy uncertainty has broader macroeconomic consequences. It says the impact on GDP begins to appear from the second quarter after uncertainty rises and continues through the fourth quarter.

“As policy uncertainty increases, GDP declines. The analysis suggests that higher uncertainty reduces GDP by around 2 percent,” says the report.

Real imports also fall significantly, declining by about 15 percent, while private sector credit contracts by around 5 percent. Unlike the stock market, however, the effect on lending appears with a delay.

The report found little evidence that policy uncertainty has a significant impact on the consumer price index, suggesting inflation is less sensitive to uncertainty than other macroeconomic indicators.

The findings reinforce a message that economists have repeatedly highlighted in recent years: stable and predictable policies are essential for sustaining investment, strengthening private sector confidence and supporting economic growth.

The central bank study recommends that policymakers adopt clearer, more transparent and more predictable fiscal and monetary policies. It particularly stresses the need for consistency in sensitive areas such as the capital market, arguing that avoiding abrupt policy shifts would help improve investor confidence, reduce market volatility and support broader economic stability.

articles.title: ‘There is still fire in me’: How Abhishek Bastola is battling administrative neglect to keep Nepal’s tennis dream alive
articles.summary:
On October 25, 2023, while competing at the Davis Cup in Isa Town, Abhishek Bastola was battling more than just Qatar’s top player, Mubarak Alharrasi—he was also fighting a fever and a runny nose. Frequently reaching for his towel between points at the Bahrain Tennis Federation court, Bastola displayed remarkable grit to win the match in straight sets.

After a brief half-hour break—spent refueling on fruit he’d brought from his hotel—Bastola returned to the court, teaming up with Aki Zuben Rawat for a doubles match against Alharrasi and Rashed Nawaf. The physical toll finally caught up with him; as soon as the match ended, Bastola collapsed.

“I vomited all over my t-shirt,” Bastola recalls. He returned to his hotel to wash the poor-quality garment himself, as it was one of only two he had for the entire tournament. “I had to wear that same shirt for my match the next day.”

Bastola and Rawat were then accompanied by Pradip Khadka and Ritik Rana. It was the first time that Nepal participated in the Davis Cup, dubbed the World Cup of tennis, organised annually by World Tennis.

The following day, Nepal faced Yemen, where Bastola swept aside then-Yemen No 1 Ghassan Al-Ansi in straight sets. He maintained his momentum throughout the tournament, overcoming a second-set stumble to defeat Abdulla Faaih Fazeel—the Maldives’ top-ranked player—on October 28, 2023.

There are currently 160 countries in the Davis Cup. The countries have been divided into five groups—Groups I and II consist of top countries, while those in Groups III, IV and V fall in the lower levels.

Nepal competed in Group V during their 2023 debut. With three singles victories that year and a matching performance in 2024—defeating top players from Guam, Brunei, and hosts Bahrain—Bastola was instrumental in securing Nepal’s promotion to Group IV.

Despite his pivotal role, Bastola was surprisingly excluded from the national squad last year. In his absence, Nepal failed to win a single match and was promptly relegated back to Group V.

“I don’t know the exact reason for my exclusion last year,” Bastola says with a wry grin from his current training base in China. “But one thing was certain: the Nepal Tennis Association didn’t want me on that team.”

For Bastola, this exclusion was not a new experience. Rather, it was a familiar disappointment for an athlete long accustomed to being denied both institutional support and professional opportunities.

“I have been participating in global events without a single penny—either from the state or the NTA,” Bastola, who has represented Nepal in over 20 countries, told the Post during a phone interview following his Friday evening training session. “Neither my travel, accommodation nor gear have been supported… In fact, the only official recognition I received at home after my historic Davis Cup victories was a Thakali dinner.”

Bastola is currently in Tianjin, China, for an event under the Men’s World Tennis Tour. Bastola is the only Nepali to be playing in the tour of World Tennis, the global governing body of tennis formerly known as the International Tennis Federation (ITF). He has an ITF Ranking of 1,270.

Bastola reached China from Bengaluru, India, where he played in an event of the UTR Pro Tennis Tour. He played five matches there—against India’s Keerthivassan Suresh, Suraj R Prabodh, Gandharv Gourav Kothapalli and Neeraj Yashpaul, alongside Norway’s Baltazar Wiger Nordas. But he could only manage one win, coming from behind to defeat Prabodh 4-6, 6-2, 6-3.

To qualify for the UTR Pro Tennis Tour, a player must rank among the top 3,000 globally. And Bastola is the only Nepali to fall under the standards to date.

His first serve

Bastola, now 28, first picked up a racket as a young child in his hometown of Pokhara. He began by following his father to the local courts, where the elder Bastola played the sport recreationally.

Yet, his passion for the sport wasn’t immediate.

“I was quite good at cricket and now feel I could have excelled in almost any sport I chose,” says Bastola, reflecting on his naturally athletic childhood. “But I found solace in tennis because of its steep learning curve. It’s far more demanding than it looks—you have to maintain absolute focus and grind through matches for hours.”

That dedication paid off quickly. By age 15, Bastola was already dominating Nepal’s domestic circuit, and by 17, he was representing his country on the international stage at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon, South Korea.

“It may be because my parents were athletes themselves that they have done everything they can, and even beyond, to help me fulfil my hunger in tennis,” Bastola said. “They are the only ones who made me what I am today. I remember my father allowing me to do wall practice at our garage when I was a child.”

His parents, Anuj Kumar Bastola and Padma Bastola, were former national badminton players who met and fell in love on the badminton court before getting married.

By the end of his adolescence, Bastola had outgrown the domestic circuit. He was practically unbeatable at home, yet he found himself at a crossroads, yearning for a challenge that could match his ambition. This search for higher-level competition eventually led him to the United States in 2018.

His early success, including representing Nepal at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon at just 17, paved the way for his next chapter. These accolades earned him a full scholarship to Saint Mary’s College of California, where he balanced the rigors of academia and elite sport, graduating with a degree in Business Administration in 2020.

“I competed in the NCAA Division 1 for college,” he says. “It is the highest level of competitive college athletics in the United States.”

For the past six years, Bastola has been striving to establish himself as a full-time touring professional, yet the climb to profitability in pro tennis remains brutal.

“It is virtually impossible to earn a proper livelihood from tennis unless you are ranked in the world’s top 100,” Bastola explains. “When millions are competing globally, reaching that bracket is extremely tough.”

Opportunities and support denied

Bastola vividly recalls the stinging frustration surrounding the 2019 South Asian Games, an event Nepal was preparing to host on home soil.

“I was in Kathmandu then. And I wanted to compete at the South Asian level as a medal was in sight,” he remembers. “But I had to play the qualifier, which I would have easily won. The qualifier was not organised unless I was in Nepal. It was organised once I reached the US.”

Bastola alleges that the NTA intentionally manipulated the schedule to block his participation. “It was a deliberate move to make way for someone else—that is simply how sports administration functions in Nepal,” he adds.

He was equally devastated when he was not taken to the Davis Cup last year.

And a similar scenario was about to repeat this year as well. “I was almost denied a spot in the 20th Asian Games taking place in Japan in September,” he says.

Undefeated on domestic courts for nearly a decade, Bastola qualified as Nepal’s No 1 at the 18th and 19th Asian Games in 2018 and 2023, respectively. But he had to fight off the court to get a slot for the 20th edition.

“The NTA asked me to return to Nepal to play selection trials to be eligible for the 20th Asian Games. I declined because it would have been a waste of critical time and training,” Bastola said. “I am competing globally—in fact, I am the only Nepali tennis player doing so—and there is no one in Nepal who can beat me. When I asked if the NTA would cover my travel expenses for trials, they refused.”

Unwilling to miss the Asian Games, Bastola took his case directly to senior national sports authorities, explaining his situation and track record. Officials eventually exempted him from flying back for trials. And he is currently spending out of his pocket to participate in the events in India and China, all so that he can reach Japan at his current peak and put up a good fight against far better opponents.

“The association [NTA] has always worked for the benefit of the players. Abhishek is no exception,” says Manohar Das Mool, who was elected as the president last year. “We know how good of a player Abhishek is. But he also needs to follow the rules. If we had any problems with him—despite him keeping accusing the association—why would we be taking him to the upcoming Asian Games?”

Regarding further support, the association gets a Rs300,000 budget annually from the National Sports Council, Mool says. “What can we do with that amount?” he questions. “We hope Abhishek keeps growing as we want him and all our players reach greater heights and we have been trying it by managing extra resources and funds.”

The dream of playing at a Grand Slam

Currently, world’s No 1 Jannik Sinner has the highest Universal Tennis Rating (UTR Rating) of 16.40 among pro men, followed by Carlos Alcaraz (16.31) and Alexander Zverev (16.15).

In the UTR Rating, all players are rated on the same 1.00-16.50 point global scale based on daily match results. Bastola has a UTR Rating of 12.07.

“The UTR Rating is the best way to measure yourself against all other players regardless of their age or skill level,” says Novak Djokovic, a 24-time Grand Slam champion.

Bastola has also traded shots on court with Djokovic when the legend was in California for the BNP Paribas Open-Men’s Singles in March 2025. “I was then recruited as a hitting partner for the participating players like Djokovic to train,” he recalls with a sense of big achievement. “I felt extremely lucky then. I also met Alcaraz then. And I am glad I could click pictures with them.”

Meeting Djokovic and Alcaraz firsthand only reinforced Bastola’s ambitions.

“I have always aimed to compete at the highest levels, but meeting two of the best in the game gave me extra motivation,” he said. “Still, I constantly wonder how far I can realistically reach while doing this all on my own.”

For Bastola, the ultimate goal remains qualifying for Grand Slam main draws—the Australian Open, Roland Garros, Wimbledon and the US Open.

Asked what it would take for him to reach those heights and put Nepal firmly on the global tennis map, Bastola pointed to administrative reform: the national association needs leadership driven by authentic passion for the game and real investment in player development.

“I always speak up when I feel there is something wrong. And it has only backfired in terms of the support and recognition I deserve,” Bastola told the Post. “But I won’t change. I will keep moving forward to becoming the best player I can. There is still a lot of fire in me.”

articles.title: The persistent cycle of hope, expectation and dismay in modern Nepal
articles.summary:
Some notable features of modern Nepali history include the praxis of transition as well as people’s expectations, hopes and frustrations. This is indeed a feature of transition in the world. But in Nepal, as history shows, stories of dismay and unfulfilled expectations are mixed with dreams of change. We can see this pattern if we consider the major transitions that have occurred in the latter decades of the 20th century and the first two decades of the 21st century.

The transitions are notable for a few reasons. Political scientists, politicians (except a few) and social scientists have studied this subject. Many seminars and research projects are conducted, and academic theses are written on this phenomenon of transition in Nepal. It is beyond the scope of a short take and the subjective perception of a literary academic even to outline them. I want to share my personal impressions about the praxis of transition and the pattern of adjustment that recurs at intervals in modern Nepal. People of past generations saw and even experienced a number of praxes, and the younger generations have experienced a few of them. They have created some, we can say, as in the latest example of the Gen Z uprising.

The focus of every transition, interestingly and remarkably, is the people and the question of their rights. Every transition has projected people’s rights and bears testimony to their violations. An important instance has occurred in modern Nepali political and social history. This is surprisingly overlooked by both political parties and historians. I want to begin with a remarkable court hearing that is historical in a number of ways: BP Koirala’s court testimony in 1977. Following King Mahendra’s coup and the dissolution of Parliament in December 1960, Koirala and his colleagues, including Ganesh Man Singh, were put in Sundarijal prison. After his release in 1968, BP chose to go to India with his colleagues. He spent several years there before returning to Nepal in 1976 for some reportedly compelling reasons. Arrested again, BP was tried at a makeshift court.

It is important to revisit one important aspect of that testimony in today’s Nepal, when the question of people’s dignity in this country has become a motif of discussion. The testimony that BP gave in court is a very important political document that evokes the system of justice and democracy. There, BP questioned the legality of his arrest and the audacity of the king to strip the people of their democratic rights by dissolving the Parliament they had elected. A great theatrical or dramatic quality was in that court testimony, something that those working in theatre, including me, thought should be staged.

It was difficult to find this important document even among Nepali Congress people, which dismayed me then. A professor of political science, Krishna Khanal, gave me a photocopy of the document, based on which I wrote a play titled Sandajuko Mahabharat that was staged at Village Theatre under the direction of an NSD Delhi theatre graduate, Bimal Subedi. It was an entirely non-partisan theatrical exercise. Academic Sanjeev Uprety brilliantly played the role of BP alias Sandaju, and theatre artist Suryamala Sharma played the role of Sushila Koirala. Other young generation theatre artists successfully played the rest of the roles. We could not perform the play even for a month because of the Indian ‘embargo’ imposed under the order of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. That made it impossible for the audience to find public transport to come to see the play.

The highlight of the court hearing of BP is the written testimony he gave in court. Referring to the royal coup, BP said in front of the jury—the day the king staged the coup in December 1960, millions of Nepalis felt that they had lost their prestige; they felt demoralised. And that was a serious blow to the human rights and dignity of the people. I do not want to cite other arguments that BP Koirala presented at the court in his own defence as an individual defendant and a lawyer. That was the first time when a lawyer, a freedom fighter, had pleaded at the court on behalf of the entire people of Nepal. The question of prestige and the phenomenon of demoralisation deserve special mention today when Nepali people are fighting for the same.

That court hearing and the question of the dignity of people is the mantra of Nepali popular historical uprisings. But there is a pattern of people’s frustration that appears after every political transition in this country. The time of transition naturally brings euphoria, which does not last in that shape for very long. History shows that some patterns of people’s frustrations have some common roots. For a widely cited example, the system gets mired in practices commonly called corruption, indifference and injustice. After every shaking political change, people naturally wait for their government to come up with good plans and visions of amelioration.

But the experience shows that even realistic expectations of people are not addressed. Maitighar Mandala becomes agog with demonstrations of many groups who travel long distances to become visible and put their grievances to successive governments. That principally includes corruption, the settlement question, betrayal by moneylenders, educational conundrums and, most important of all, a sense of losing prestige or dignity. This may remind us of absurd plays staged by actors who are not heard and, painfully, they know that.

Many historical events have occurred in Nepal in the 21st century. One important element of these praxes is the transition to democratic rule. The present multiparty republican constitution, which may require necessary reviews and amendments in the course of time, represents a solid example of the spirit of transition. The diverse approaches to political change meet at a common platform. The Parliament is such a forum where the erstwhile Maoist guerrillas, the Nepali Congress, the various factions of the communists of Nepal, the advocates of the abolished monarchical system, and, more recently, the Rastriya Swatantra Party, which won a majority in the general election and includes Gen Zers, all meet and discuss, though this does not appear to be happening as expected. Judging by the praxis of change, we can say that democratic history has not ended in Nepal.

articles.title: Lift the migration ban on domestic work
articles.summary:
Nepal remembers women migrant domestic workers exist when their remittances arrive home. However, it forgets them when they seek support from the state. Somewhere in West Asia, a poor Dalit Nepali domestic worker is fulfilling the care needs of a household. Driven not only by gender- and caste-based oppression at home but also by the lack of economic opportunities in the country, she sustains households in the Gulf, contributes to Nepal through remittances, helps her family escape intergenerational caste oppression, and invests in the next generation of Nepali citizens.

While she is legal in the country where she works, she is invisible in the country to which she ‘belongs’, having migrated without the government-issued ‘labour permit’. By refusing to recognise her labour migration, the state has chosen to evade its responsibility towards her, thereby rendering her disposable.

Nepal’s migration bans on domestic work push women into precarious and undocumented journeys, making them invisible to the state that bears a constitutional duty to protect its most marginalised citizens. If she suffers exploitation, abuse, disappearance or even death, the state has no official record that she ever migrated. It excludes her from consular protection, accountability and pathways to redress against exploitation. In effect, she is punished for navigating the very deficit in state care, opportunity, welfare and protection from gender-based violence that thousands of women confront every day.

Yet for 25 years, successive governments have waged a war against women’s migration into domestic work whilst failing to confront exploitation within that sector. They have mistaken Nepali women’s mobility for the problem, turning some of the most marginalised citizens into the targets of state restriction and confinement. Their solution has been to prevent Nepali women from migrating, resulting in successive bans on domestic work migration.

However, research from Nepal and countries such as Sri Lanka, Indonesia, the Philippines and Bangladesh challenges this assumption. It shows that migration into domestic work is neither inherently nor exceptionally exploitative. Instead, exploitation is embedded across migrant labour regimes, with male migrant workers from these countries experiencing exploitation that is often comparable to, or even more severe than, that experienced by women domestic workers.

Research suggests no ban can stop determined Nepali women from migrating. The ban prevents the state from knowing about their migration, abandons thousands of women who are working as domestic workers, and absolves the state from being obliged to respond when things go wrong.

More recently, Nepal imposed a blanket migration ban in 2017. This total ban on migration for domestic work followed a field visit by and recommendation from a parliamentary committee. These parliamentary committees carry institutional weight, but their decisions are not fixed; they can revise recommendations when new evidence or circumstances demand it.

For example, the committee in 2020 recommended seven preconditions for lifting the migration ban, the most important being the presence of a dedicated Bilateral Labour Agreement (BLA) on domestic work with a host country. In practice, this has functioned as an indefinite postponement, since most of the preconditions lie largely beyond what Nepal can secure on its own.

These preconditions have become an instrument of state abandonment, enabling the government to evade its constitutional obligations whilst thousands of already marginalised citizens continue to bear the consequences.

Even where BLAs exist, they have not delivered what is claimed. Nepal already has BLAs with several destination countries where migrant workers continue to face degrees and forms of labour exploitation and abuse. Hence, a signed agreement alone cannot guarantee safe working conditions.

Nine years on, we now have a substantial body of evidence about what the ban actually produced: growth in irregular migration, greater exposure to abuse and exploitation, invisible and premature deaths, and the denial of safe and regulated employment to thousands of women. This evidence should prompt a parliamentary committee to revisit earlier recommendations.

Consider the numbers: In the first 10 months of the last fiscal year, 1,273 Nepali migrant workers returned home in coffins. Of these, 1,229 were men and only 44 were women. These figures cover only migrants who travelled through formal channels; the deaths of women who migrated informally are not counted at all. Nepali men’s deaths in sectors such as Qatari construction have occurred at a comparable or greater scale, yet this has never led to a ban on men’s mobility. Only women’s migration into domestic work has been treated this way, an asymmetry that traces back to the 1985 Foreign Employment Act, which required women to obtain a male guardian’s permission to migrate.

Yet, the ban fails to keep Nepali women at home. Estimates suggest that between 60,000 and 100,000 Nepali women currently work as domestic workers in the Gulf, most through informal channels, and this may understate the actual figures, given how much of migration in domestic work is invisible.

An ILO report suggests that when the ban was briefly lifted in 2010, the proportion of women migrating through legal channels tripled. This highlights that women are migrating at similarly high rates, only now without a labour contract, registration with Nepali missions abroad, consular assistance and any route to compensation if they are injured or killed.

Civil society groups, returnee workers and concerned Nepali citizens should consider a formal route open to them now: a petition to the Women and Social Affairs Committee and the Law, Justice and Human Rights Committee, requesting a review of the ban on the grounds of women’s rights, labour migration, human rights and access to safe employment. This migration ban must be revisited in light of nearly a decade of evidence showing that it has failed to serve the purpose for which it was designed.

None of this suggests domestic work abroad is free of risk, or that bilateral agreements and other preconditions have no value. BLAs, embassy capacity, recruitment reform and compensation systems should be built after the ban is lifted. For nine years, these preconditions have allowed the state to wash its hands of thousands of marginalised Nepali women who care for families abroad and sustain households at home through remittances, yet officially do not exist as migrant workers in the eyes of the state to which they belong.

The committees that recommended this ban in 2017 acted within their authority and, one assumes, in good faith. Parliament cannot continue claiming to protect women whilst defending a policy that leaves thousands beyond the protection of the Nepali state. Hence, the choice before Parliament is whether it will accept responsibility for a policy that has exposed thousands of Nepali women to abuse, exploitation and death, while making their suffering invisible to the very state responsible for protecting them.

articles.title: Learning AI, unlearning AI
articles.summary:
I spent two years learning about artificial intelligence-based tools. I read the papers, tested out the models, attended the workshops, built prompts, compared outputs, and watched each new release with the excitement of someone witnessing the future unfold in real time. Like many people working close to technology, I believed AI would become the defining aspect for our generation.

Then, I spent one year unlearning AI. I realised how astonishing these systems had become. I also realised that the greatest threat AI posed was not to my career, but to my mind. This latter realisation came when I uninstalled ChatGPT from my phone.

My friends assumed I was making some grand statement against technology. But I was simply trying to rescue a part of myself that had begun disappearing. The habit of turning to an AI tool starts innocently enough. You want to Google something, so you ask ChatGPT. You struggle to begin writing an email, so you ask ChatGPT to write it for you. You cannot quite articulate a thought, so you ask ChatGPT for help. Eventually, the question stops being “what do I think?” and becomes “what does AI think I should think?”

I had spent years believing AI was merely another tool. But tools usually help us do things better. Generative AI, on the other hand, offers to do the thinking before we have even attempted to do it ourselves. And most of us avoid admitting how dangerous this bargain is. For centuries, good education has been built around a simple principle: struggling with an idea so you can make it your own. Every confused student, rewritten paragraph, abandoned draft, and wrong answer contributes to the better understanding of things. AI offers us a world without this essential friction and, by extension, without the process of thinking. Psychologists call this cognitive offloading, which means to shift mental effort onto external tools (in this case, generative AI).

As one would expect, after deleting ChatGPT, my life became slower. The first few days, I absentmindedly swiped through my phone looking for the app. But eventually, I began spending longer browsing through the internet. I also spent a considerable amount of time talking to people. I found myself reading instead of seeking summaries. Tasks which once took an hour now consumed entire evenings. For a while, I feared I had become less intelligent.

But soon I started remembering things again. My ideas stayed with me because I had earned them. My arguments became sharper because I had built them myself. I stopped confusing instant access to information with genuine understanding. Most importantly, I started writing again. Not just generating text; actually writing.

Writing has never been about arranging words into grammatically correct sentences. It is instead the slow and often frustrating process of discovering what one actually believes. Every first draft is a conversation between conflicting ideas; every revision is evidence that one’s mind is growing. Generative AI skips all of that and delivers polished conclusions without any intellectual struggle. Some term this efficiency, but it is actually intellectual outsourcing. Somewhere along the way, we began celebrating people for producing more instead of thinking better. Students submit essays they never wrestled with. Marketers publish campaigns they never conceived. Professionals proudly announce that AI writes their emails, prepares their presentations, and even generates their reports.

We have become curators of machine-generated thoughts instead of authors of our own. The most worrying aspect is that this dependence feels rational in isolation. Why spend three hours writing when AI can do it for you in 30 seconds? Why read an entire book when a detailed summary can be generated? Why struggle through uncertainty when certainty is so accessible? But uncertainty is where thinking happens. That very uncertainty and the struggle that comes with it are doing something an algorithm can’t: they are helping us develop our intellect.

Every meaningful belief I hold today was shaped by confusion that was followed by clarity. Every article I am proud of began as an incoherent mess. Every worthwhile conversation I’ve had forced me to reconsider assumptions I wasn’t even aware I harboured. None of these could have been “prompted” into existence.

People often ask whether I have tried Claude, Gemini, or whichever new AI tool currently dominates the headlines. The truth is that I have not. But the question should really be: what kind of person do I become if I allow a machine to perform the very activities that shape who I am? Thinking is not merely a means to an answer. It is how we construct our own identity.

I increasingly believe history will remember this era not as the moment machines became capable of writing, but when humans voluntarily stopped trying. That, to me, is infinitely more tragic. We are told that AI will free us to focus on higher-order thinking. But everywhere I look, the opposite is happening. After all, AI tools encourage us to surrender the very habits from which higher-order thinking emerges.

Perhaps the saddest consequence is that we no longer trust ourselves. Faced with an empty page, many people's first instinct is not to think but to ask a chatbot about what they ought to say. We have begun borrowing confidence from machines because we no longer believe our own imperfect thoughts are enough. I now refuse to live that way; to become a second-hand thinker in my own life. I would rather write a flawed article than publish a “perfect” one that I cannot really claim ownership of. I would rather forget, search, revise, and begin again than slowly surrender the most human thing I possess: my ability to think.

-The Daily Star (Bangladesh)/ANN

articles.title: The parliament that cannot question its prime minister
articles.summary:
Late night on Tuesday, India’s Congress MP Shashi Tharoor stood up in the Lok Sabha with nine minutes on the clock. The bill under debate was India’s anti-paper-leak law. Tharoor’s point was engaging and harder to dismiss: the country’s public examination system needs structural reform that prevents leaks, rather than relying only on harsher punishment once the damage is done. Right then his mic was cut and the House moved to other business. But it didn’t really matter. Tharoor had built the argument anyway, on the record, in the shape a policy debate is supposed to take and it was covered widely in the Indian media.

The next afternoon, in the same chamber, opposition leader Rahul Gandhi produced a different kind of moment.
